objective: Total knee arthroplasty rehabilitation per the 2026 APTA guideline: range-of-motion work instead of continuous passive motion, progressive strengthening, motor function training, and early daily quadriceps NMES

sources.cite: APTA. Physical therapist management of total knee arthroplasty: revision 2026. Phys Ther. 2026;106. doi:10.1093/ptj/pzag058 (PMC13403188)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11 in the Europe PMC full text. Physical therapists should not use continuous passive motion after primary, uncomplicated TKA (high quality, strong); should include passive, active-assistive and active ROM exercise (moderate); should apply NMES to the quadriceps at least daily, started early, at the highest tolerable intensity (moderate). Team members should be aware of complications that may affect exercise, including thromboembolism.

parts.label: Measures and interventions
parts.criteria: Measures knee flexion and extension with a goniometer, quadriceps (extensor lag) and girth; plans ROM exercise (passive, active-assisted, active), progressive strengthening, gait training, and quadriceps NMES at least daily at the highest tolerable intensity; does not plan CPM.
parts.modelAnswer: Goniometry for flexion and extension, a straight-leg raise for extensor lag, knee and calf girth on both sides. Heel slides and knee bends, quad sets, straight-leg raises and mini-squats, gait training with the walker, and NMES to the quadriceps at the strongest intensity he tolerates, daily. No CPM.

parts.label: When to stop and call
parts.criteria: Names DVT signs (calf pain, tenderness, swelling of about 3 cm or more versus the other side, warmth, pitting edema) as a reason to stop lower-limb exercise, score the Wells criteria and contact the surgeon the same day for a scan; names sudden breathlessness, chest pain or falling SpO2 as a reason to call 911.
parts.modelAnswer: If he has new calf pain, tenderness, warmth, pitting edema or a calf 3 cm bigger than the other, I stop the leg exercise, score the Wells criteria and call his surgeon today for a duplex scan. Sudden shortness of breath, chest pain or a falling saturation means 911.

expertPath.text: Ask about new symptoms including the calf; measure knee ROM, extensor lag and knee and calf girth on both legs.
Quadriceps NMES at the highest tolerable intensity; heel slides and knee bends; quad sets, straight-leg raises and mini-squats.
Gait training with the walker, checking RPE; try a cane if he is steady. No CPM.
Screen first: a calf ache since last night. Measure the calf (4 cm larger than Monday) and examine it (warm, tender, pitting edema). No exercise, no walking, no massage.
Wells 4, likely. Call the surgeon's office with SBAR for a same-day duplex scan; teach the warning signs of a clot and a lung clot.

referredSameDay.headline: Progressed, then scanned the same day
referredSameDay.body: You moved his rehab on with guideline doses, screened before loading the leg on Thursday, and turned a likely Wells score into a same-day scan. That is the expert path.

referredNoRehab.headline: Scanned the same day, no progress on Monday
referredNoRehab.body: The clot was handled well. Monday needed more: ROM and strengthening exercise, gait training and strong NMES, not a CPM machine.

referredGaps.headline: Referred, with gaps
referredGaps.body: He got to his surgeon, which mattered most. Look at when you screened, whether the leg was loaded or massaged after the signs, and who made the call.

peCaught.headline: A lung clot, 911 called at once
peCaught.body: Your response to the emergency was right. The lesson is upstream: a screen at the start of Thursday's visit would have found the calf before it came to this.

peMissed.headline: A lung clot without a 911 call
peMissed.body: The most useful kind of run to learn from. Sudden breathlessness and chest pain after surgery mean stop, sit him upright and call 911.

sentHome.headline: Sent home with an untreated clot
sentHome.body: Calf pain, swelling, warmth and tenderness after surgery need a Wells score and a same-day call, never a massage and a home program.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: The run reached its time limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Monday: measure flexion and extension with a goniometer, extensor lag and girth on both legs (a baseline); give ROM exercise (passive, active-assisted, active), progressive strengthening, gait training, and quadriceps NMES at least daily at the highest tolerable intensity; do not use CPM. Thursday: screen before loading. New calf pain, a calf 4 cm larger than Monday, warmth, tenderness along the deep veins and pitting edema give a Wells score of 4 (surgery within 12 weeks, calf swelling 3 cm or more, localized tenderness, pitting edema), so DVT is likely: stop lower-limb exercise, do not massage, and contact the surgeon the same day for a duplex scan; mobilize again once anticoagulation is therapeutic. Teach the warning signs. Sudden breathlessness or pleuritic chest pain means 911.

peWhy.ask: While the paramedics are on their way: what most likely happened?

choices.label: Part of a calf clot reached his lungs (a pulmonary embolism)

peWhy.explain: Two weeks after a knee replacement, a swollen tender calf followed by sudden breathlessness and chest pain that is worse on breathing in points to a pulmonary embolism. That is why calf signs get a Wells score and a same-day scan before the leg is loaded.
